title: Colic, as UNICEF describes frequent long crying
summary: UNICEF describes colic as frequent long crying, more than three hours a day on three days a week for at least one week, with unknown causes, usually easing by six months.
body: UNICEF Parenting says colic is when babies cry frequently for lengthy periods. The pattern it gives is crying more than three hours a day, three days a week, for at least one week. It says the precise causes are unknown, that colic is common in many newborns, that it can start at a few weeks old, and that it usually goes away by six months. The page says there may be little to do besides trying to comfort the baby, and it says to contact a health care provider if the baby keeps crying a great deal, if the caregiver is worried, or if coping is difficult. Those figures are UNICEF's description. They are not a diagnosis this card applies to a baby.
